utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be the next question that I would like to deal with, Your Honours. But in view of the fact that we haven't got a translation of this document, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you. I asked you to read out. You read out a certain line, which is -- which the Chamber cannot understand without being informed about the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I again read what you read. "The next night." Which night was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking me, Your Honours, according to what the witness stated, it would be the 20th. Because he was brought in on the 19th. That's why I asked him when it was that he was exactly brought to Susica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the permission of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at this moment. I'm trying to clarify matters. So you said that the night of the 20th apart from -- but that's how you interpret it. "... Nikolic beat up Galib Smajlovic and Dzevad Saric who succumbed to the blows." Could you now read the -- is this inconsistent with what was said in paragraph 42 and 44? Is that what your view is?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not going to say that it is inconsistent but it's undefined, because in P207 the witness says which persons took Mr. Saric out and nothing more than that, except for him hearing screams. In the statement of the 27th, the witness says that the following night Nikolic beat up Saric and that he succumbed to the blows, not saying who it was that took him out. My question has to do with this difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. There's no inconsistency. You just want to explore what the basis of the witness is on certain matters. Don't put non-existing inconsistencies to the witness. Ask the questions which you would think would clarify the matter. We are at the time where we usually take a break. Mr. Stojanovic, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honours, I will fit into those two hours that I had envisaged. And my colleague from the Prosecution also had the extra 15 minutes this morning. But now I'd like to deal with Batkovici and some questions that are inconsistent in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My questions -- my question was: How much more time would you need? Because you were not granted the two hours. I said before the last break that you had one hour left because you paid so much attention to irrelevant and mainly background information. How much time would you still need, Mr. Stojanovic? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes are granted. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 17 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if -- we would first like to have the witness escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I would like to -- one second, please. One of the statements was with a translation. I think that was 1D00261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was 260. That is the statement given to the Lukavac War Crimes Bureau. Mr. Stojanovic, is that an official translation? Because I noticed that exactly on the relevant line there was a slight difference between what our interpreters gave us compared to what is in the written translation. Therefore, I'm asking you whether the translation you provided is an official translation or an unofficial translation. And if it's an unofficial translation, by whom it was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this translation with ER markings we received from the EDS, and I cannot say who the author of the translation is, but we got it from the system, and it's not our translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, could you please try to find out whether that translation is generated by Prosecution or by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: We are. Just a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Osmanovic. Sorry for being so impolite not to address you when you entered the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic will now put further questions to you, but only after Ms. D'Ascoli has provided us with further information.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I just wanted to confirm that we have the request translation and it is an official translation provided from the OTP. Well, meaning, requested from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because I'll deal with it at a later moment and not in the presence of the witness. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall try to fit within the time allocated to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, we'll be dealing with the part of your testimony that relates to Batkovici. You got there on the 30th June 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned persons whom you remember mistreating prisoners.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You gave us the names of Fikret Smajlovic, Dzemal Zahirovic, and Esad Bekric?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to know is were they there as prisoners or on some other mission?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours and Mr. Stojanovic, they were there as prisoners. Dzemal Zahirovic, also know as Spajzer or Django, is a Roma born in Zenica, and I happened to first see him in Vlasenica in the Susica camp. The other one was from Brcko municipality. He wore camouflage trousers and he acted as some sort of chief among the prisoners. Esad Bekric was also brought in a uniform. Somebody said he was part of the so-called Tuzla column, that he was from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that before the cantonal court in Tuzla there was a trial and Fikret Smajlovic was found guilty and convicted?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about his being convicted, but I know that he had been taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that against Dzemal Zahirovic there was also a trial before the cantonal court in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday in response to a question from the Prosecution you mentioned - and that was page 2766, line 10 of yesterday's transcript - you said that after the mistreatment Ejub Smajic was one of the men who died. You remember that question?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that man, where he was from?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was brought from Bijeljina, together with Zlatar. We were told he was from Bijeljina and that he had a private catering business.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see his mistreatment or killing?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him beaten up every day, and I saw him dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask, Your Honours, that we see in e-court 1D267. And before we see this document, I should like to inform you that it is an indictment we received last night from Bijeljina against four persons relating to the events in the Batkovic camp and the proceedings that are ongoing against these persons. Unfortunately, we have it only in B/C/S, and I will read some representative passages out. If we could see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this document - and this is an indictment issued by the prosecutor's office in Bijeljina against four persons - these persons are charged, among other things, you can see this in the middle, with beating the following people, the most badly: Ekrem Cudic; Husein Cudiz, known as Zlatar; Ferid Zecevic, known as Professor; Alija Gusalic, nicknamed Konjanik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you start reading documents, again they're not available in English, shouldn't we first ask the witness whether he's aware of any proceedings, what light he could shed on it? It's unclear to me what direction you would like to go and I'd like to know. So let's first ask whether the witness is aware of any ongoing proceedings at this moment before the court counsel just mentioned that is in Bijeljina. Are you aware of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, whatever is there in the proceedings, Mr. Stojanovic, ask him anything you would like to ask him. But let's first see whether you can ask these questions without referring to court documents. And I could imagine that if they are relevant at any point in time that, if there's no objection to from Prosecution, that you would bar table them sooner or later as information about proceedings ongoing in Bijeljina. But let's focus with this witness on what he can tell us about whatever event, and if there's any use in them putting to him what is found in the proceedings in Bijeljina, you could consider that. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for this suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I mentioned some names, including the one you mentioned, Ejub Smajic, known as Mesar. My question is: In view of what you stated in P207, is this consistent with your knowledge that these people were beaten the most badly while you were at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, for instance, I don't see the name of Fadil Alihodzic, son of Ismet, from Vlasenica, known as Praga.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the eighth name on the list.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, his name is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this passage of the indictment is consistent with your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at the next page of this indictment which says, among other things, the middle, these persons succumbed to the beatings: Husein Curtic, Ferid Zecevic, Ilijaz Okanovic, and then another three names. And it says Ejub Smajic suffered serious injuries. Would this indictment convince you if I say that you were wrong and you did not see Ejub Smajic succumb to the injuries from the beating in your presence?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will not convince me, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you still claim that Ejub Smajic from Bijeljina --

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Died from the beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this part of the indictment is not true.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it's not uncommon that the content of an indictment is challenged. That happens now and then. But what I'd like to have is the line you referred to to be read out -- or to read that out exactly so that the Chamber is aware of what the document actually says. Could you please read out the relevant line before the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the record, Your Honour, I'm reading from page 3 of the indictment, which reads, inter alia: "While serious injuries were sustained by the following: Ejub Smajic, aka Mesar, Sabrija Mehmedovic, and Nedim Mustacevic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With your leave, after this response from the witness, we would like to call up in e-court 1D268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- let me just check first. Have you told us already who were the persons who were indicted? I'm trying to find that. Because you said this is an indictment issued by the prosecutor's office in Bijeljina --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 1, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- against four persons. And they are, you say, charged with, and then you mentioned who, according to this indictment, were beaten. But we do not know yet who were indicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Your Honour, under count 1 of the indictment the following are charged: Petar Dmitrovic as warden of the camp; Djoko Pajic as a warden in a later period; Djordje Krstic as deputy warden; and finally, Ljubomir Misic as shift leader among the guards. And that is described on page 2 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see in e-court 1D268. Your Honours, while we're waiting, it is a document this Defence team obtained through the cantonal prosecutor's office in Tuzla. As you can see from the header, it is dated 16 August 2004, taken by the prosecutor's office from Witness Ejub Smajic. You can see the witness's personal details below in the document. He was born in Bijeljina in 1949. And in the following pages, he describes all that he went through at Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you again, Mr. Osmanovic, would this record of a witness statement convince you that your memory is not right when you say that Ejub Smajic was killed by the beating before your eyes at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the same person, Mr. Stojanovic, I will not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Osmanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is an ambiguous answer. Because you say, Mr. Osmanovic, "if we are talking about the same person," you would not agree. Do I understand your answer to be that you leave it open that it may be another Ejub Smajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you're actually saying, it may well be another person and that is the reason why it does not convince me. Is that the gist of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll conclude with this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in Batkovic, did you ever hear of the existence of two individuals called Ejub Smajic from?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that there two Ejub Smajic, but from people from Vlasenica and Bijeljina -- Vlasenica municipality said that there were two men in Vlasenica who had the same first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was clear. You did not hear that in the prison in Bijeljina there were two men who had that same name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of any such thing, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Let me try to understand. You said your question was clear, Mr. Stojanovic. You asked the witness whether, while he was in Batkovic, he ever heard of the existence of two individuals by this same name. The answer was: "I didn't hear from that, but from people from Vlasenica and Bijeljina, they said that there were two men in Vlasenica who had the same first and last name." So what the witness is telling us is I heard that but not in Batkovic. Then you asked: "You did not hear that in the prison in Bijeljina there were two men who had the same name?" Did you mean to ask whether he heard it in the prison of Bijeljina, or whether there were two persons in that prison with the same name? What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked him, Your Honours, and I'll repeat my question, whether, while he was in Batkovic, he heard that there were two individuals called Ejub Smajic from Bijeljina, whether he heard that at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never heard any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, at the same time I heard him say -- at least that's what I read in his answer, he didn't hear that, that was about a question which was limited exclusively to what he heard in -- what he heard in Batkovic. But he said that he heard about two people with the same name but he heard that at another occasion. Is that how I have to understand your answer? That, at any point in time, perhaps not in the prison or not in Batkovic, that you were -- that you heard about two people with this same name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said that I heard that there are people who have the same first and last name in Vlasenica. This concerns two individuals with the same first and last names. The only difference is in the name of the -- the father of these two individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if you say two people with the same name, you refer to Ejub Smajic as the -- no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not referring to Ejub Smajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's in general you say you have heard about a person -- two persons with the same name but not directly in relation to persons by the name we see in these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Mladic would like to consult with counsel. Please, at low voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With Your Honours' leave, I would now to have a look at 1D266 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this to appear on the monitor, sir, I just have one question I would like to put to you. Would I be correct if I said that the maltreating you were subjected to in Batkovic came to an end in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question. In August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In August 1992 did the maltreating, your maltreatment cease then?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August 1992 I was still an inmate in the Batkovic, Mr. Stojanovic. However, the people who went to perform labour, to dig trenches, fell trees, and so on and so forth, these individuals were not subjected to the same beatings, to the same extent. There were daily beatings, Your Honours, of people who were in the Batkovici camp every day, who had to be present for the evening roll-call, so to speak. They were all beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you don't mind, I'm short of time.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Those who went to perform labour, am I to take it that they were more privileged than those who remained behind in the camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who went to perform labour, Mr. Stojanovic, were more privileged when it comes to the beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me if I said that the leadership, or those in command of Batkovici, replaced the guards and brought in other guards who treated you fairly. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned from labour, there were new guards there. I don't know what the reason for this was, but the guards who had appeared were fairer. They had come from Bijeljina and the surroundings of Bijeljina, and they behaved more decently than the other guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to draw your attention to the witness's statement, 27th of July 1992. It's the last paragraph in the B/C/S version, page 2, and it's the last page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, you gave this statement on the 23rd of July, 1993, after the change in the security organ of the ABiH 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the right page on our screens? The second page you said, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's the second page in the B/C/S version. The last paragraph on that page. And it's page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I ask if it's P207 or?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 266. 1D266. You have it on the screen. Could we have a look at page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Could you please point at what paragraph we are supposed to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we need the B/C/S version on the screen. We have only two English. Now, there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have -- again, there is two English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the last paragraph in the B/C/S version, on page 2 of the B/C/S version. And could we please have page 3 in the English version. Page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you have read through it. You say: "In August 1992 " --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which paragraph? Where do we have to look? We have a whole page and you expect us to find in half a split second --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 7 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The paragraphs are not numbered. Paragraph 7 on this page? There are no seven paragraphs on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be of assistance --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 3 from the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Exactly. Because I saw a reference to August 1992 in the third paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Yes. That paragraph. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say: "In August 1992, the guards in the Batkovici camp were changed. Most of the guards who beat us, maltreated us, and brutalised us were replaced." You mention some names, and then you say: "They were replaced by a group of elderly villagers from the village of Batkovici who treated us fairly so that there were no more beatings. There was no more maltreatment, but we to do hard labour as before." Very briefly, do you stand by this part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just one more question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, were you just seeking confirmation of what the witness testified already? Because I do not see a new element in it. If the witness testifies about a positive change in the treatment, then there's no need to go to a statement where he says exactly the same. Please proceed. And I do see that you read Batkovici. I'm looking at the original. It looks as if the English translation which refers to Ratkovici is wrong, although the original is not very clear, but I take it that the replacement was by elderly people from Batkovici. But we could ask the witness to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The village of Batkovici, the camp of Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to say that I like to tender 1D266, because the statement P206 isn't contained in it. I also want to have marked for identification, since we don't have any official translations, 1D267, the indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, let's take them one by one. You want to tender which one first?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D266. 1D266, which is this witness's statement dated the 23rd of July, 1993. It is the statement that we were commenting on just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is -- is that the last one you used? The one on our screen? And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's only for the purpose of establishing that he said, the same what he testified today? And then we have the whole of the statement into evidence, which we have not looked at, and the only purpose apparently being that he said so before. Do the parties agree that the general improvement of treatment at that point in time in Batkovic also is reflected in his statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we will have to look into it. Because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we read the relevant portion. Would you agree that that is more or less the same as what the witness said, that in the last period of time in Batkovici, that they were treated better.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I -- we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So therefore there is no need to have this statement in evidence - is there? - Mr. Stojanovic. I have got no idea what is, apart from this three lines you pointed at, what is in the statement. So would you agree that there's no need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honours, in the statement provided by the Prosecution, 92 ter, according to the 92 ter procedure, nothing is mentioned about this. That's why I'm asking this to be admitted. I can suggest -- I could suggest that only this part of the statement be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the witness testified to that. You asked him was the situation at the end better? Were you better treated? Yes. Especially those who had to go for work were treated better. So, therefore, we don't need the statement. We have the testimony of the witness, isn't it? And you're perfectly entitled to elicit the evidence from this witness, and you did so because it does not appear in the Prosecution statement, but why have it in both clear answers to clear questions and then have it again in a statement? I mean, there's no dispute about the statement confirms what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you still want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, because the statement doesn't only contain this part. I had other questions about this statement, and the Defence team would be grateful if the entire statement could be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- what questions did you put in relation to other parts of the statement? I think you only drew our attention to this specific part. The Chamber has no idea about what else you dealt with, which is found in this statement, which we haven't read. And if you've asked the questions about it, if it's consistent with what he said in the statement, then we have his testimony and we do not need the statement anymore. But -- correct me when I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I tender this, I ask to put one more question before I tender this into evidence. Our right is to tender documents and your right is to admit them or not. As for this statement that you say you haven't read, it is our legitimate right to tender it into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admission is denied. The only portion that was put to the witness is exactly about the same matter he testified about before, and the Chamber has not heard or have been -- nothing else in this statement has been brought to our attention, so therefore the evidence of the witness is clear without this statement and apparently fully in line with it. Please proceed. Next one, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The next question I wish to put you, Mr. Osmanovic, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were at this moment tendering documents. I would like you to continue with that because we have now dealt with 1D00266. What's the next document you would like to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next two documents are the documents that we used with this witness, 1D267, the indictment of the district prosecutor's office in Bijeljina; and document 1D268, the record of Ejub Smajic's testimony before the cantonal court in Tuzla. I suggest that these two documents be marked for identification because we don't have official translations yet. We have asked for them and we will be receiving them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 1D00267 will receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit D47 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is marked for identification. 1D00268.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit D48, Your Honours, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That document is marked for identification. Mr. Stojanovic, were all the other documents you used either tendered or do you not wish to tender them?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that I used, P207 has been admitted into evidence, Your Honour, and the statement from the 27th of July has not been admitted into evidence. I haven't used it and, therefore I'm not going to tender it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 27th of July, you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I think you said that 1D00261 was not admitted. That is not the case. It was 1D266 which was denied admission. As far as we are concerned, it seems that you have used 1D00260, statement of Osmanovic, the War Crimes Bureau in Lukovac, which has a translation, but you have not tendered that as far as we are aware of. Do you wish to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes. So I shall repeat. 1D260, the statement from the 4th of October [as interpreted], 1993, we would like it tender into evidence. As for 1D261, the statement from the 27th of July, 1993, we are not tendering into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have to decide on 1D260. You -- did you misspeak when you said the 4th of October? That is how it appears on our transcript. Whereas, it's my recollection - and also on the list - that it was a statement given the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The statement is from the 4th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 1D00260 receives ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes D49, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D49 is admitted. You wanted to put one last question, Mr. Stojanovic, if I understand you well, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. It's going to be a question to corroborate what was stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Osmanovic: Would you agree with me that when you were leaving the Batkovici camp, about 250 detainees were left there and most of them were from Prijedor, Kotor Varos, and Kozarac, and when speaking to these detainees, you were told that they were members -- or, rather, most of them were members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but that they did not dare disclose that, and that when Kozarac fell these combatants cast away their weapons and were taken prisoner as civilians. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you put a composite question with four elements in it and then to say "yes or no," that is bad advocacy. We take it one by one. Is it true that when you were leaving Batkovici that 250 detainees were left, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I left on the 30th of June, when I went to Tuzla, when I was exchanged, a certain number of people stayed behind who had been brought from Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- have you spoken to these detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did speak to someone of these people, Your Honours, and I never talked to others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did they tell you that they were members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, even who was a member of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had to hide that very carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's not what I asked. Did they tell you that they were members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not recall at this point in time anyone having said that to me then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they say anything about -- that they were, as combatants, that they had thrown away their weapons and that they were taken prisoner as civilians? Did they say anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember, Your Honour. For the most part, we talked about how they had been brought there from Manjaca. Because, by then, the camp of Manjaca had been disbanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Stojanovic, we have now -- you put your last question, we translate it into five questions, and they have all been answered. No further questions? That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, with my leave, Mr. Stojanovic? More questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall leave with a sense of bitterness if I do not say this. The question that I put is a quotation from this witness's statement from the 23rd of July, 1993, 1D266, that has not been admitted into evidence. I did not put these questions. I did not invent this. I put the text to him, as stated there. If you allow me now, because there's discrepancy between the witness said today and what he said in his own statement of the 23rd of July, 1993, with your leave, with all due respect, I would like to tender 1D266 yet again. Because there is this discrepancy, so we would like to have this admitted into evidence. Of course, the decision is up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, leave out your bitterness, Mr. Stojanovic. You could have asked the witness all the elements of what is found in that statement, and if you say they are inconsistent, you could have put to the witness what he said earlier. No problem with that. But you can't just put such a composite question and ask for a yes and a no. We have, I think ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have put to the witness that this was his statement, matters would have been totally different. I would not have intervened as I did. Now let me just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, please ask for the document to be put on the screen, choose the right page and the right portion, and ask the witness the questions which are, of course, appropriately to be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please have in e-court 1D266 yet again, the last page, or page 3 in B/C/S, and the last page of the English version, the third paragraph from the back, Your Honours. I'm going to ask for the last page in English as well, the third paragraph from the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page -- page 3, second linea from the bottom, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go one page back in English. This is the relevant page, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to ask you in accordance with the instructions. Mr. Osmanovic, is it correct that when you went for the exchange 250 prisoners stayed in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot say exactly how many people were left, 200, 250 approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these prisoners mostly came from Prijedor, Kotor Varos, and Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people introduced themselves as having been from these municipalities, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When speaking to them, were you told that most of the prisoners from Kozarac belonged to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but that they did not dare disclose that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were stories that were circulated amongst us, the detainees. As you can see from this statement here, I did not say such and such a person said this to me, but what I say here when speaking to the other prisoners, I was told ... So I worked and we would come back from our labour only when there were exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were told that when Kozarac fell, these combatants threw away their weapons and were captured as civilians?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was being said about this alleged fall of Kozarac, Mr. Stojanovic. I did not spend much time with these people. My colleagues who were in the Batkovic camp every day had more time and spent more time with these people, so this was just sort of an internal conversation that we had. Because I would be away from Batkovic camp for three or four months. I was in the Ugljevik prison, in the prison in Lopare. I also worked, was involved in labour in these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Osmanovic, those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, bearing in mind these answers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd like to tendered it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And we have no objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Chamber admits into evidence 1D00266, I think it is. Madam Registrar, it would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit D50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D50 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, if you would have dealt with the matter right away, then we would not have had to first deny it and then, on the basis -- we did that on the basis of vague references to portions of the statement we had not read, and, on the whole, I think, for the next time, it would have been better to start with the substance and then only with the background. We take a -- no -- yes. We have to take a break anyhow. How much time would you need, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I would have one question only, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question only. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am looking at the Defence at this moment. There is one question from the Chamber. One question from Ms. D'Ascoli. Would we try to finish that in the next three or four minutes or should we take the break first? The short breaks, after one hour, are at the request of Mr. Mladic, so I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely because of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To continue for five minutes? Or to take a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mladic's proposal is that we do take the break, Your Honours, so that would be our proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back for one more second after the break, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I use the time. When I asked about the translation on a matter which was considered to be inconsistent, one of the translations - and I think it's the written translation - says: "... succumbed to Chetnik torture and beating by Zoran Viskovic," whereas the oral translation was "died after having been tortured and killed by the Chetnik, Zoran Viskovic." Or the other way around, but there is some difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Osmanovic. Therefore, I would like to have that translation. You can find that in the transcript and to have that portion of the translation to be verified again.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Osmanovic, Judge Fluegge has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Sir, you were asked this morning -- was it this morning or yesterday? I forgot. Just a moment. This morning. About Rade Milic. You will recall the situation with a war and with the unknown person in the car. You were asked: "The information about Rade Milic is something you did not mention in your earlier statements; correct? " And then you said: "I didn't mention Rade Milic because that man acted as a professional towards all of his neighbours." Is this Rade Milic the person unknown to you who was sitting in the car you mentioned in your statement in paragraph 17? Is it the same person or another person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a different person, Your Honour. The unknown person who sat next to me in the car was a man called Rajkenovic, whereas Rade Milic is the brother of a neighbour of mine. He spent a lot of time in the neighbourhood and he lived there for a while, and he acted in a very correct manner towards me and all those people who were taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I asked you this question, and please help me with that, because counsel for the Defence stated then, and this is on page 31, line 9 to 11, and I quote: "So in your earlier statements where you described this event, you did not provide full information. Instead, you said it was an unidentified uniformed member of the police?" Now, I take it that this -- Rade Milic was not the unidentified uniformed person in the -- in the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No, that's not him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You had one question, I did understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, I just have a question about the Ejub Smajic. Defence counsel earlier today asked you about him and you said at temporary transcript page that you saw him beaten up every day, and I saw him dead. Can I just ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're referring to temporary transcript page, if you would give the number, then we could --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Didn't I say it? Oh, I'm sorry. Temporary transcript page number 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Line 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Osmanovic, was just if you could describe what you saw exactly when you say him dead. And, again, I'm referring to Ejub Smajic.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Batkovic camp consisted of two hangars -- in fact, at the beginning there was one hangar and two tents, and later on a second hangar opposite was also put up. We saw his dead body to the right of the tent next to the gate, and that dead body was said to be Ejub Smajic who died from the beating. In the same place Zulfo Hadziomerovic was lying as well, and all those dead were driven away from Batkovic camp. To clarify. Batkovic camp was surrounded with a wire fence that we put up and it had two gates. The guards used one gate, and the other gate was for prisoners who were taken out to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And only two follow-up questions. So you said: "We saw his dead body to the right of the tent next to the gate..." Did you mean that you saw the body lying on the floor, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the concrete.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, yeah, last point. Who said it was Ejub, Ejub Smajic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoners. We never got any information from the guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions in that respect as well. Did you know anything about Ejub Smajic apart from that other prisoners said that this was him lying dead? Do you know where he came from? Do you know what his age was? Do you have any -- any further details about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that if you say it was Ejub Smajic, you say a prisoner, which was referred to you as Ejub Smajic, which you could not verify because you didn't know anything further, that that person you saw lying on the ground -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is at least clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, have the questions by the Prosecution or the Bench triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood correctly, Mr. Osmanovic, in response to a question from Honourable Judge Orie, you said you knew nothing about Ejub Smajic but his name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told it was Ejub Smajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Aren't I right if I say that you had stated you knew Ejub Smajic was from Bijeljina and a caterer by profession?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was just brought to Batkovic camp, I was told that he was from Bijeljina, and they mentioned his occupation, and that his nickname was Konjanik, but I didn't know any of these people at the time. I did not know the others who got killed at Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you heard from Ejub Smajic was from Bijeljina and that he had a catering business?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Your Honours, could we see 1D266 concerning the questions put by Judge Fluegge. This is now Exhibit D50, second paragraph on page 1 in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind paragraph 17 of P208 -- P207, you say that Bastah, Dragan Deuric, son of Zoran - a name you corrected during proofing, you say now it's Goran, son of Zoran - and a third uniformed man I didn't know came to my door, without mentioning any car. Now in response to a question from Judge Fluegge, you say three men came, two of them wearing reserve police uniforms and the fourth one was in the car?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Do you mean to say that when, in this statement of 23rd July 1993, you said that Bastah, Deuric, and a third man I didn't know in uniform came to my door, behind that phrase "third man I didn't know" is the man in fact whose name you didn't want to mention?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing is hiding -- hidden, Mr. Stojanovic. Bastah opened the door. I saw a man behind him and a third man with his back to me. When I got into the car, I saw yet another man. And Rade Milic was standing on the concrete service in my yard and that's the person I didn't want to mention, because that man was a very fair and decent one and I don't want him to have any problems because he was so fair and decent to his neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague says that on page 77, line 16 of the LiveNote, something is written that the witness did not say, and I would like to get a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, of course. May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- the man whom you met in Batkovic with the nickname Konjanik, was he killed at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was only beaten at Batkovic camp. They beat him on charges that he had tried to enter a cafe in Bijeljina on horseback. I did not see that but I saw him being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not see him killed in Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. As far as I know, Mr. Alija Konjanik is alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And he has nothing to do with the person you knew as Ejub Smajic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you tendered 1D00268 and it has been marked for identification under number D48. And you described it as a statement dating the 16th of August, 2004. Now, it appears to me that in e-court has uploaded two documents, I think, both most likely witness statements. The one dated the 16th of August; but the next one, the 16th of September. Is that correct? And did you intend to tender two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You are perfectly right. 16 August 2004 is the first statement given to the cantonal prosecutor's office in Tuzla by Ejub Smajic, and his second statement is four years later, 16 September, 2008, also given to the prosecutor's office in Tuzla in preparation for the issue of the indictment against these four persons for the events at Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would have appreciated if would you have referred to this document as consisting of two documents which -- of which only one of them dates from what you indicated. Could you take care that it is, with priority, translated so that the Chamber can look at the whole of the document, especially in order to be available to verify whether it is possible that two different persons are involved. No further questions? Then this concludes your testimony, Mr. Osmanovic. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, less time left than we would have expected but nevertheless still some 20 minutes. You had suggested to deal with a few procedural matters and you're invited to introduce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There are four matters that the Prosecution would like to raise with the Chamber. Two of them -- the first one would be that I would like to make a submission with respect to witness Mr. Osman Selak who will give evidence next week. Ms. Bibles would like to address the Chamber with respect to D43, an exhibit tendered by the Mladic team, and she would also like to address Mr. Ivetic's complaint about when he had notice of the exhibits the Prosecution would use. Finally - and, Your Honours, I think that I would probably have to post-pone this until next week - I would like to make a -- the progress report with respect to the filing of 92 bis and quater motions. So, Your Honours, if I could begin with the witness next week and if I could ask the assistance of the Chamber to hand out a page to the Chamber and to the Defence, it'll -- it's an example of what I'm proposing so that the Chamber, I think, may better understand when I explain my proposition. Your Honour, Osman Selak was a career member of the JNA. In 1992 he was a colonel, and then the VRS was formed Mr. Selak remained an officer in the VRS for some time. The Prosecution has given notice it intends to ask the witness about a number of documents. The primary evidential value of these exhibits is the information they contain on their face. The witness is able to address the authenticity of the documents as well as provide general evidence about particular categories of documents, their purpose and function. Such evidence will enable the Chamber to more fully understand the import of these and other documents in the case. In a few situations, he will be able to place a particular document in the context in which it was drafted. The Prosecution makes the following proposal as a more efficient way of dealing with this limited and unique situation, and the handout that's now before you is an example of what this might look like. We would propose that after Mr. Selak arrives in The Hague this coming Saturday that the Prosecution provide Mr. Selak with the binder of the exhibits that we have given notice we may use with him and that we provide the chart that gives him space to record two types of observations. One column would allow him to provide any observation he has with respect to authenticity or function of the document; the other column would be a place in which he could report any substantive comment he may wish to make about the document. The document would then be translated and provided to the Defence. During the witness's testimony for the most part, the Prosecution would limit its examination regarding it -- regarding the documents to simply eliciting evidence about the chart and then tendering the underlying exhibits. The Prosecution would reserve the tendering of the chart and exhibits until after the close of the cross-examination so that the Defence would have a full and fair opportunity to ask any questions they wished regarding the creation of the chart or the underlying documents themselves and make full submissions with respect to their position regarding the chart and the documents. I submit that substantial time may be saved next week by proceeding in this manner. That concludes my submission in that regard, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I see Mr. Lukic is not here, lead counsel. Do you want to make any submissions at this moment on this suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honour. It sounds reasonable to us. My colleague, Mr. Lukic, is now preparing the witness we are discussing, Mr. Selak, and since there was a change in the schedule and the witness on Monday is mine, I would be happier if Mr. Lukic could answer on Monday about this method of work with Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask if Mr. Stojanovic would have any objection to us proceeding in this fashion with the witness pending a final determination by the Chamber. Of course, should it be decided that we would not proceed in this way, we would, of course, still disclose any comments that the witness made with respect to the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I see you're nodding no, which I understand to be that there is no objection against provisionally proceeding in this fashion with the witness. That is hereby on the record, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, of course not yet provided with the comments by the Defence, at this moment also has no objection against proceeding as you suggest, Mr. Groome. Of course, a final determination will be made after we've heard from the Defence whether we can proceed in this same way in court as well. Having dealt with this, next item. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, there were a couple of exhibit issues that I wanted to just briefly go back to. First, I did tell the Trial Chamber I would take a second look at D46. I have confirmed that that was based on ITN footage and therefore I was correct in not objecting to that. That issue stands. I did determine that I did not tender an associated exhibit which I had intended to do, that was 65 ter 22391, which -- I realise Mr. Ivetic may not be in a position to look at, but that was an associated exhibit which is a video of the Prijedor Crisis Staff meeting. There was discussion about the video and I would simply move to tendered it at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I verified in e-court that that is video in question. No objection to that associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A surrogate sheet has been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript have been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number of 65 ter 22391 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P212 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the next exhibit that I would like to address is D43. This is the clip that was used by the Defence to confront the credibility and recollections of Mr. Vulliamy regarding the sounds of the fire-fight during the transport to Omarska. And this clip was played at 2634, I believe that was a Wednesday. Your Honours, Mr. Vulliamy was subjected to several -- many pages in the transcript with respect to his impressions about this event. He was specifically confronted with this video and advised to listen specifically to the actual ambient sounds of the fire-fight. Yesterday the Chamber invited the Prosecution and the Defence to try to reach an agreement as to the authenticity of this particular exhibit. To that end, the Prosecution has done some very basic analysis of this video, and it has been compared with the sounds and the scenes contained in P203. Based on that initial analysis, it is the position of the OTP that the sounds of the fire-fight in D43 were added to this video-clip which makes it, in the OTP's position, a clearly fabricated soundtrack on this video. It also appears from our initial analysis that the original sequence and speed of this footage has been edited. Based on our initial review we are submitting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think parts of what you said is missing. "It also appeared from the initial analysis that..." The previous line, I think a few words are missing on the transcript which may have been caused by your speed of speech. Could you read line 21 of page 84. You said the video has been edited. That's what we read, but I think you said more about what in this video was edited.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Your Honours. The original sequence and speed of the footage. And thank you, I had not caught that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I missed that. So therefore, could you slow down in order to avoid that it happens again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours. Your Honour, based on this initial review, we are submitting the video for external forensic analysis and we will obviously provide a report of that to the Chamber. Having stated this position, the Prosecution will make available to the Defence this initial analysis. We would invite the Defence to review that as well and state its position with respect to Exhibit D43. I do want to advise the Chamber that at this point I do not now object to D43 coming into evidence. However, the Prosecution considers that the purpose of this evidence is not the truth as purported by the exhibit. Rather, so that the Chamber can take his evidence and consider evidence of fabrication if additional evidence is proffered from the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that your submission in relation to this video?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any immediate response to that or would you like to think about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Nothing further to add until we see the preliminary analysis of the Prosecution. We've got nothing, I don't think, about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Bibles, apart from how you finally will proceed, would it not be wisest that if this material is submitted for forensic analysis that it's done in such a transparent way that any matter which would be of interest to the Defence would immediately included in any further analysis - again, if it ever comes to that - so that we don't have to do it in two rounds? I see, Mr. Ivetic, that that at least meets no objection on your part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to be updated as soon as the Defence has received and made up its mind on the -- on this matter. Mr. Ivetic, the analysis, the preliminary analysis is already on paper? Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, what we have is a DVD which has the actual comparisons in several different formats, and we will provide that to the Defence this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be fair to ask the Defence to respond to within a week. Would that be?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that's fair, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we -- that then deals with this matter. Any further matter, Ms. Bibles?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just one, Your Honour. I would like to clarify the record regarding the Chamber's guidance and the list of exhibits which were provided to the Defence in this case. The Chamber's guidance was articulated on 4 September 2012 at transcript page T2160. That is: "The Chamber would except that a first list of documents be sent no later than seven days prior to the witness's testimony. Such a list could then be complemented at a later stage following any proofing of the witness." So that the record is clear, the Defence was given an initial list of exhibits, identified by 65 ter number, that might be used with Mr. Vulliamy on 13 April 2012 with a filing relating to witnesses. This was a list of nine associated exhibits and 33 potential non-associated exhibits. Given the breadth and scope of this witness's experience and testimony, this was a very reasonable list. By comparison, as cross-examination began with this witness, the Defence provided OTP a list of 25 documents as well as various video-clips, just to show the comparison. Given that we provided a list of documents so many months ago, I was very surprised on Wednesday when Defence counsel said at transcript page 2573: "We did not receive the list of documents to be used in direct examination for this witness until less than 48 hours before his scheduled testimony." When I pointed out that the first list of potential exhibits had actually been provided months before, Mr. Ivetic responded, in part, by saying: "Many of these were exhibits that had nothing to do with this witness that I did have to review and I did go through and I did eliminate." I have now gone through and reviewed thorough the originally list sent on 13 April which was identical to the list sent on 4 May. I can describe that 33 of the 33 non-associated exhibits, 13 were media articles or releases, either by the witness, involving the witness, or of his evidence. Seven were transcripts or notes relating to the 1996 interviews of Stakic and Kovacevic. Five were photographic stills taken from the ITN film, two were maps of Prijedor, two were hand drawn sketches by the witness. There was a map of the Dayton Agreement areas, a video of Loznica, Omarska, and Trnopolje, one military report, and one ICTY witness statement of Mr. Vulliamy. In the final analysis we were able to reduce this initial list down from the 42 to 16 plus the transcript. I'll reiterate that at that time Mr. Ivetic also stated: "There were exhibits that are now on the list that were not on this original list that was sent in May of 2012." That statement didn't comport with my understanding at the time, but I wanted to make sure of the facts before I responded. In fact, there were no additional exhibits added to those notice to the Defence months ago. One exhibit, which is now P200, is a six-minute clip from a video -- was extracted from a video which was included on the original notice. There were no additions to the original list with respect to this witness. Your Honours, I was very concerned about the Chamber's concerns about the seriousness in which I or others of the Prosecution were taking the Court's guidance. Your Honours, the Prosecution in this -- with this particular witness continued to narrow the field of examination dramatically. This is evidenced by the fact that the direct examination time in fact came in considerably under the original estimated time. I can advise the Court that we are actively trying to focus our issues with witnesses and make good use of our courtroom time. We continue this narrowing process, frankly, even once we get into the courtroom. We believed that we were acting in the spirit of co-operation when we narrowed the original list, and on Monday advised Defence counsel of that fact and provided them with a specific narrowing. This was for a witness who was taking the stand on Wednesday. And finally, Your Honours, the Prosecution takes your guidance very seriously. We act not only to follow the letter of the Chamber's guidance but the spirit of co-operation. I specifically, as well, take the guidance from this Chamber very seriously, and I was very concerned by the record that was left on this matter, and I felt it was important to clarify the record regarding the actions with respect to this witness and of the Prosecution. I very much appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. We have no time to further discuss the matter. There seem to be two relevant and important issues remaining at this moment, though one is whether when Mr. Ivetic said that most of the documents have got nothing to do with the witness or with the testimony of the witness, whether that was accurate or not. Ms. Bibles has, at this moment, given an explanation as how, in her view, they really had to do with the witness. The next remaining item is whether the narrowing down of your exhibit list was really depending on the proofing of the Witness Vulliamy or whether that could have been done at an earlier stage, we still have not heard an explanation why this reduction could have been done only two days before the witness testified. These are, in my view, the two matters remaining at this moment which we'll not discuss, because we're already over time. The parties should consider whether they want to make further submissions or whether they want to leave it as it is, or to agree on what, on their own -- on -- on their mutual positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I spoke too quickly. The Chamber expects a response on the first issue from the Defence. So therefore, we really would like to hear from the Defence why they stated that the matters -- that the documents were unrelated to the -- to the -- to this witness. Mr. Ivetic, when do you think you could give such a response?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Monday, Your Honour. If I had the document that I had yesterday, I could read you the numbers and could pull them up in e-court and see what they're related to, that they're not related to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if there is no other matter, we adjourn and we will resume on Monday, the 24th of September, 2012, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.
